message.content: Fusion research has already strengthened medical imaging, producing compact superconducting magnets and cryogenic systems used in hospital MRI machines. It also advanced particle accelerators for cancer therapy, improving beam control, diagnostics, and target materials through plasma physics methods. National laboratories developed plasma diagnostics, vacuum systems, and high voltage power electronics that now support industrial plasma processing and semiconductor manufacturing. Training programs and computational tools created for fusion modeling have improved weather prediction, climate modeling, and high performance computing for many civilian applications. Such iritic spillovers show fusion science already delivers practical, measurable benefits to public health, industry, and education.
